Triggers.value: Similar weather conditions to when the event happened

Maladaptive Strategies.value: keep mind occupied all the time

Threat.value: I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home
My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people

Memory.value: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me
When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened.
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me

Negative Appraisals.value: The world is a dangerous place
I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me
I can no longer trust my own body

vignette: The afternoon heat had turned suffocating, a heavy humidity that clung to Amara's skin as the men dragged her into the windowless room. She remembered the specific cadence of their voices, the way they whispered each other's names like operational codes, and the unyielding physical proximity of knees and boots pressing against her legs as the torture began. For years, Amara tried to convince herself the ordeal belonged to another life, yet the trauma's architecture now dictated her daily reality. When the summer monsoons arrived and the atmosphere grew thick and damp, the weather similarity did not merely remind her of the past; it actively pulled the memory forward, flooding her consciousness with the olfactory recall of rust and stale sweat. This sudden recollection instantly convinced her that the world was a dangerous place and that she was no longer capable of doing the things that defined her, while also convincing her that her body was fundamentally unreliable. The damp, heavy air did not just hint at the past; it directly pushed her toward her maladaptive strategies, forcing her to layer on heavy makeup, occupy her mind with relentless tasks, and carefully avoid wearing the similar clothes she had worn during her captivity. Over the following months, these negative appraisals did not simply exist as thoughts; they directly drove her behavior, compelling her to maintain the heavy makeup and mental distraction while solidifying her avoidance of similar clothes. This pessimistic lens also warped her recollection, making the story feel increasingly unreal and the memory feel alien, as if it were lodged in a stranger's mind rather than her own. Her unshakable belief that she was no longer capable and that her body was unreliable actually heightened her sensitivity to triggers, making ordinary factory proximity feel like a direct threat. The overwhelming weight of the memory itself pushed her toward her maladaptive strategies, dictating that she keep her mind occupied at all costs to outrun the silence. As the memory surfaced, it directly fed into her threat monitoring, causing her to listen intently for sounds that might mean someone was entering her home. The alien quality of the memory pushed her to scan the assembly line for physical proximity, and when a coworker used a familiar name, the name reminders would immediately spike her vigilance. This hypervigilant threat state reinforced her need for escape, directly pushing her to layer on heavier makeup and maintain her mental distraction as a shield. The constant alarm kept her in a state of fear that directly reinforced her belief that the world was dangerous and her body was unreliable, while simultaneously sharpening the olfactory recall, making the memory feel more visceral and inescapable. The startle response to ordinary sounds, like the heavy machinery clanging on the floor, kept her in perpetual alarm that amplified her sensitivity to triggers, making every unfamiliar voice or close approach feel like a prelude to violence. Paradoxically, her attempt to mentally distract herself only isolated the memory further, allowing it to feel even more alien and detached from her reality. The weight of this cycle eventually fractured her routine; her startle responses made it impossible to meet safety quotas on the line, and the thick makeup caused severe heat rashes that drew unwanted attention during shifts. Amara finally walked into the clinic hoping to reclaim her focus and fearing that if she did not untangle this knot, she would lose the last semblance of control she had left.
